title: UFO whistleblowers beg Trump for immunity so they can share 'alien secrets'
excerpt: Three leading UFO whistleblowers have formed a coalition urging the US President to grant them immunity and waive lifelong NDAs so they can share alleged evidence of ETs
content:
Three leading UFO whistleblowers have formed a coalition urging the US President to grant them immunity and waive lifelong NDAs so they can share alleged evidence of ETs

13:05, 21 Sep 2026

UFO whistleblowers are begging US President Donald Trump to grant them immunity so they can reveal what they claim are “alien secrets” locked behind lifelong government gag orders.

‌

‌

Three of the most high-profile figures in the so-called disclosure movement - David Grusch, Dylan Borland and Matthew Brown - have formed an unprecedented coalition urging Trump to waive their non-disclosure agreements (NDAs).

‌

They claim they gathered information while working inside highly classified programmes but are legally barred from sharing it publicly without White House intervention.

‌

Filmmaker and disclosure advocate James Fox told the New York Post: “For the first time in history you have a direct public plea, not private . . . to the president of the United States, to have their NDAs waived and have them protected, so they can disclose what they know to the American population, because they feel like it’s that important that everyone should be entitled to know that we’re not alone.”

Fox added: “You’ve got some heavyweight whistleblowers willing to reveal what they know. All they need is immunity from the president. Just the stroke of a pen. He’s got the authority to do it.”

Matthew Brown, an independent contractor for the defence industry, came forward on the Weaponized Podcast earlier this year with claims about a secret programme he called Immaculate Constellation, which he says collects UFO data across the government.

He said: “The NDAs I signed prohibit me from publicly disclosing classified information obtained through my national security work without prior written government authorisation, and that obligation lasts for life.”

He added: “President Trump has the opportunity to uproot the source of deep-state corruption, reset international relations, and lead humanity into a new era of awareness and discovery by disclosing one simple fact: we are not alone.”

‌

David Grusch, an Air Force officer who worked as an intelligence official at the National Geospatial Intelligence Agency and the National Reconnaissance Office, testified to Congress in 2023 that the US government has run secret UFO crash-retrieval programmes for decades, the New York post reported.

“Mr. President, give us the authorisation and we’re ready to go,” Grusch said in a video released by Fox. He reportedly claimed the evidence he has seen is “jaw-dropping”.

‌

He said: “This included photographs and video of the [recovery] operations including the craft and the non-human occupants. And I’ve seen this evidence with my own two eyes.

“I am prepared to provide a full historical accounting to the National Security Council . . . and the White House Chief of Staff and make any supporting public statements that are authorised.” Borland, an Air Force veteran, told Congress in 2024 he witnessed a huge triangular UFO hovering and manoeuvring over a NASA hangar before vanishing at speed.

‌

Borland told the New York Post: “Disclosure has to come from [President Trump]. He needs to rip the Band-Aid off himself and needs to go out there and confirm we’re not alone.

“We’ve recovered materials and entities - biologics.” The pressure has coincided with rapid administrative moves.

Reports say the Pentagon issued a targeted legal waiver under instruction from the Trump administration, suspending administrative and civil penalties for people who hold classified information about Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAPs).

‌

However, it does not mean whistleblowers can simply dump classified files online - they can only submit material through official channels.

A central declassification project called PURSUE (Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters) has also been set up, allowing whistleblowers to provide data behind closed doors to authorised representatives, who will vet and scrub it for national security before any public release, as per the New York Post.

Despite the releases, the White House has reportedly confirmed there is currently no “presidential speech acknowledging aliens” scheduled - but the coalition insists that with immunity and a waiver, they can finally put what they claim is physical, non-human evidence into the official pipeline.
